focus: Audit the skill-advisor brief as a per-prompt payload across all runtimes
noveltyJustification: Seven findings add scoring-to-payload, ambiguity, compiled-route, fallback, and cache/dedup evidence; one partially refines the prior size baseline into safe conditional/cache options.
keyQuestions: How does the advisor payload expand, cap, fallback, cache, repeat, and vary across runtime transports?
What safe trim, conditionalization, and cache options preserve routing value?
answeredQuestions: Established model-visible label counts, dual-threshold/no-match behavior, representative and bounded costs, OpenCode-only compiled-route expansion, warm-only fallback behavior, and recomputation-versus-delivery cache semantics.
ruledOut: topK or full projection means a full skill list is injected
no-match or daemon failure means zero payload
exact-prompt cache means model-visible cross-turn dedup
80/120 token cap bounds the whole payload
sandbox CLI failure proves production daemon availability
sourcesQueried: local compiled renderer and warm-only CLI probe 2026-08-06

claim: The canonical payload renders one passing skill label, or two only for visible ambiguity; it does not inject the full skill projection or topK list.
An executing shared hook with no passing recommendation emits the 763-byte directives fallback rather than zero bytes.
The 80/120 estimated-token cap applies only to the advisor prefix; fixed directives and OpenCode compiled summary are outside it.
OpenCode appends an uncapped compiled targets line separately; measured synthetic cases range from 74 bytes with no targets to 679 bytes with twenty representative targets.
Shared and OpenCode exact-prompt caches avoid rescoring but still append the cached brief on every invocation; no emitted-context dedup was found.
The local warm-only CLI probe returned exit 75 with sandbox IPC EPERM; this limits live telemetry but not source-path analysis.
Configured hook delivery remains distinct from observed receipt; Cursor's configured advisor cost must not be counted as observed per-turn cost.
Do not describe the advisor cache as cross-turn prompt dedup; it is recomputation reuse only.
